attempts.note: HL7 does not publish an OpenAPI document for R4. Probed /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger.json, /fhir.openapi.json and /openapi/ on hl7.org/fhir/R4, hl7.org/fhir/R4B, hl7.org/fhir/R5 and build.fhir.org — all 404 (fhir.openapi.json returns Apache's 300 'similar names' page listing only fhir.schema.json / fhir.jsonld / fhir.ttl).
The R4 downloads page lists definitions.json.zip, fhir.schema.json.zip, examples and the hl7.fhir.r4.core package — machine-readable, but no OpenAPI/Swagger artifact.

The HAPI public test server (the base URL in the adaptor's examples) serves an OpenAPI 3.0.1 document generated by its OpenApiInterceptor: 2973 paths but only two schemas (FHIR-JSON-RESOURCE / FHIR-XML-RESOURCE, both opaque), no application/json content, HAPI-proprietary paths ($hapi.fhir.reindex-status, $hfql-execute, ...) and a snapshot version (8.11.16-SNAPSHOT). It is one server's rendering, not HL7's, and carries no resource schemas, so it was used only to cross-check the path surface.
apis.guru lists no hl7/fhir API (2529 entries searched for 'fhir' and 'hl7').

Third-party generators/renderings of FHIR as OpenAPI exist but are community projects, not vendor-published (SKILL.md §2: a third-party copy is a lead, not a source). Followed the lead back to HL7's own machine-readable definitions, which are what this spec is built from.

HL7's own complete R4 JSON Schema (draft-06): 680 definitions covering all 146 resource types, all datatypes and all backbone elements. Saved verbatim as upstream.json and converted to components.schemas.

HL7's base CapabilityStatement for R4 ('a server that provides the full set of functionality defined by FHIR'): 145 resource types, their interactions, 1697 resource search parameters, the server-level interactions and the operation list. Saved verbatim as upstream-capabilities.json (sha256:29ae88d66f66371f97a71feece55f2464ae35e8fadf40ddb79d4a005c1a5c217) and converted to the path surface.

All 46 R4 OperationDefinitions fetched individually (https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/operation-<resource>-<code>.json) for the $-operation paths, their levels (system/type/instance), their input/output parameters and their response resource.

The normative RESTful API specification: URL shapes for each interaction, the patch interaction and the conditional create/update/delete forms, the _search POST form, and the GET-invocation rule for operations.

notes: HL7 FHIR Release 4 (v4.0.1) RESTful API. HL7 publishes no OpenAPI for FHIR, but it does publish the two machine-readable definitions this spec is converted from: fhir.schema.json (the complete R4 JSON Schema — committed verbatim as upstream.json and hashed) and the base CapabilityStatement, 'a server that provides the full set of functionality defined by FHIR' (committed verbatim as upstream-capabilities.json). 'Full' here means every one of the 145 R4 resource types with all eight interactions the base CapabilityStatement declares (read, vread, update, delete, history-instance, history-type, create, search-type) plus patch and the conditional create/update/delete forms from http.html; the four system-level interactions (transaction/batch on POST /, search-system, history-system) and capabilities on GET /metadata; and all 46 R4 operations at the levels their OperationDefinitions declare — 1872 operations over 944 paths, with all 680 upstream definitions carried across (660 named component schemas plus FHIR's 20 primitive types, inlined at their use sites). The adaptor is release-agnostic (state.configuration.apiPath picks the endpoint, e.g. baseR4/R3/R4) but its examples, its configuration-schema placeholder and OpenFn's FHIR deployments target R4, so R4 is what info.version declares. Conversion decisions: draft-06 `const` became a single-value `enum`; `type: object` was added to object definitions that only carried `properties`; FHIR's 20 primitive types (string, id, dateTime, ...) are inlined at each use site instead of being $ref'd, so they do not surface as data objects; every response and body is offered as both application/json and application/fhir+json; and the seven Resource-scoped operations ($validate, $meta, $meta-add, $meta-delete, $graph, $graphql, $convert) use a `{resourceType}` path template (enumerating all 145 types) rather than 1160 duplicated concrete paths. Operation inputs are typed as the `Parameters` resource — which is the FHIR wire format — with each OperationDefinition's parameters listed in the operation description; a GET form is emitted only where every required input parameter is primitive, per the GET-invocation rule in http.html, so $process-message, $submit, $submit-data, $convert, $transform, $match, $meta-add, $meta-delete and ChargeItemDefinition's $apply are POST-only here, as is $closure, whose own definition ('Closure Table Maintenance') says it changes server state. Not modelled: the XML/RDF/Turtle representations, server-proprietary endpoints (HAPI's $expunge, $hfql-execute and friends), bulk-data (the separate FHIR Bulk Data IG) and SMART/OAuth2 token endpoints; auth is declared as HTTP Bearer + Basic because that is what the adaptor sends (FHIR itself leaves authentication to the deployment). One extractor artifact worth knowing: every FHIR resource has a `meta` element, which the data-object extractor treats as a pagination hint, so data-schemas/index.json lists 266 second-level types (Bundle_Entry, Patient_Contact, Address, ...) as the 'resources' instead of the 145 resource types; the object set itself is complete — all 660 named schemas, including Patient, Observation and Bundle, are present as files.
